summary: Joins related buttons, with optional dividers and text labels, into one connected strip.

orientation.note: Direction of the strip. Vertical stacks the children and joins their top and bottom edges.

anatomy.name: group
anatomy.notes: div role=group in the shadow root; named by the host's aria-label.

default.notes: Direct children only. The group sets data-position (first, middle, last, only), data-orientation and data-overlap on them when the slot changes.

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: Host aria-label is forwarded to the group. Name it when the buttons together express one control (for example a split button) and the surrounding text does not.

formAssociation.note: Layout only. Buttons inside keep their own behavior.

accessibility.focusRingVisible: The focused child is raised (position: relative) so its ring is not hidden by its neighbours.

keyboard.Tab: each button is its own tab stop; the group adds none

aria: group: role="group" with the forwarded aria-label
text children are read in order as plain text
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Console warning, once per element (in every build), when the host has no aria-label. A name from an outer legend or label is not detected.

elements.summary: A thin divider between two children of a button group, mostly used between filled buttons that have no border of their own.

anatomy.name: separator
anatomy.notes: aria-hidden line; its direction follows data-orientation set by the group.

elements.notes: Must be a direct child of sb-button-group.

elements.summary: A non-interactive text or icon cell shaped like a neighbouring button, for a label or a unit inside the strip.

anatomy.name: text
anatomy.notes: Boxed cell with muted background and a border.

elements.notes: Must be a direct child of sb-button-group.

useCases.when: Closely related actions that belong together, such as previous and next
A primary action with a related menu trigger
useCases.use: a button, a sb-button-group-separator and an icon button

antiPatterns.pattern: Mutually exclusive or on/off options in a button group
antiPatterns.why: A group of plain buttons does not show or expose a selected state

antiPatterns.pattern: Unrelated actions joined in one strip
Nesting interactive controls other than buttons
antiPatterns.why: Only sb-button children get joined corners
antiPatterns.alternative: Use sb-input-group for inputs with buttons

coverage: corner radii horizontal, vertical, RTL, single
separator decorative, size, color, no overlap after it, vertical
Tab order and raised focused child
missing-name warning on the group, once

drift.realization: the visual reference removes radii with child selectors; here the group sets the button's own radius token because the border lives in the button's shadow root

drift.contract: decorative border in the border token
drift.realization: below 3:1 on the background; the cell is not a control, so WCAG 1.4.11 does not apply

coverage: ButtonGroup: 2 variant(s), Orientation (Horizontal, Vertical); read back ok

drift.contract: Size of an icon slotted in ButtonGroupText.
drift.realization: Content the person using it places (a slotted icon, image or control); the library sample shows text only.

openQuestions.question: How can the group change the corners of sb-button, whose border is inside its shadow root?
openQuestions.recommendation: The group sets --sb-button-radius on each slotted button (a four-corner value chosen from data-position, orientation and direction). Button already reads it, so no cross-shadow selectors are needed.

openQuestions.question: How are shared borders drawn?
openQuestions.recommendation: Outline buttons and text cells after the first overlap their neighbour by one border width (negative margin), except directly after a separator.
openQuestions.answer: Negative margin of one border width on bordered children.

openQuestions.question: Does the group manage focus or selection?
openQuestions.recommendation: No. Each button stays a tab stop; selection belongs to Toggle Group.
